Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the ElectroDrive Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to ElectroDrive Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Taylor Voss, CFO; Riley Kim, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Morgan Lee, Chief Technology Officer; Casey Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for ElectroDrive Motors, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record total vehicle deliveries of 152,450 units globally, representing a 28% year-over-year increase; substantial electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains across our fleet; effective cost reduction initiatives that lowered COGS per vehicle by 18% year-over-year; navigating the impact of raw material costs and supply chain disruptions while maintaining resilience; strong revenue performance driven by premium product mix; expanded gross margins through operational leverage; and clear delivery volume guidance by model positioning us for accelerated growth ahead. The launch of our Apex Terra SUV has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive impact on our brand image, with market share gains in the midsize SUV segment against competitors like Tesla's Model Y.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Taylor Voss:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue was $2.9 billion, representing a substantial 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 22.1%, down slightly from 26.3% a year ago but up sequentially due to increased production efficiencies and favorable product mix, despite headwinds from raw material volatility. Operating expenses totaled $650 million, reflecting disciplined spend on R&D and SG&A rationalization, and net income amounted to $180 million. We are in a strong financial position with $4.2 billion in cash reserves. 

Let me provide more color on our outlook. Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we are guiding revenue to $3.2 billion to $3.4 billion, representing 10% to 17% sequential growth and 35% to 42% year-over-year. This assumes deliveries of 185,000 to 195,000 units, with average selling price holding steady at $61,000 to $63,000. Key drivers include U.S. market strength at 65% of deliveries, fueled by the Inflation Reduction Act's $7,500 consumer tax credit and our qualifying U.S.-sourced battery content exceeding 60%; Europe at 25% with fleet deals offsetting currency headwinds; and APAC at 10% with LFP packs winning exports. Risks include potential port strikes, but upside from OTA software updates.

For the full FY 2024, we're raising guidance to $12.0 billion to $12.5 billion, implying 55% to 65% growth over last year's $7.8 billion, tracking to 720,000 to 730,000 total deliveries. Gross margins are targeted at 20-21% for the year, with Q4 at 22-24% and FY2025 trending to 25-27%. Key assumptions here include Q4 deliveries of 32,000 to 35,000 from our core plants at 85-95% utilization, gigacasting reducing body costs by 30%, ASP stability at $82,000-$85,000 with premium mix, and COGS declines of 12-15% to $55,000 per vehicle from $85-$90/kWh battery pricing and 75% North American content. This embeds IRA credits totaling around $12,000 per U.S. vehicle, localization mitigating tariffs, and hedging on key metals.

For FY2025, revenue guidance is $17.0 billion to $18.5 billion, a 40% to 50% growth trajectory on 950,000 to 1.02 million deliveries at a blended $60,000 ASP. This reflects full ramp of our Aurora platform with silicon-anode cells targeting 15% energy density gains and $80/kWh costs, U.S. at 60% mix, Europe stabilizing via affordable models, and APAC scaling with partnerships.

On delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 and FY2025: For our Model 3/Y equivalents, 125,000 to 135,000 units in Q4, 68% of mix, with U.S. at 65,000, Europe 35,000, China 25,000, driven by premium trims and FSD take rates over 45%. Premium S/7X models at 32,000 to 36,000 units, up 42% YoY, U.S.-dominant. CyberForge pickup at 22,000 to 24,000, ramping 150% YoY with fleet wins. NovaOne affordable EV pilots at 3,000 to 4,000 units, scaling to 80,000 in FY2025. This supports 22-24% margins and FCF positivity.

We're financing growth with our cash position, undrawn revolvers, and strong residuals. These figures are forward-looking, subject to supply risks and macro headwinds.

Next, Riley Kim will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Riley Kim:
Thank you, Taylor. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes of 185,000 units in Q3, up 62% year-over-year, and reduced manufacturing costs meaningfully.

These results stem from our four pillars of cost discipline, delivering $2.8 billion in run-rate savings, exceeding targets, and dropping COGS per vehicle to $32,500 on flagships like the NovaPack sedan, expanding gross margins to 22.8%. First, supply chain optimization yielded $1.2 billion annualized savings through localizing 65% of LFP cathode production in our Nevada CATL JV, slashing cell costs 22% to $87/kWh, competitive with BYD, and ramping 4680 cells for 25% reductions via dry electrode processes. Rare earth hedging locked lithium at $1,200/tonne and nickel at $17,000/tonne, with dual-sourcing chips cutting ECU costs 15%.

In Europe, shifting to Northvolt avoided CBAM tariffs, saving €250 million, while China verticals compressed crossover costs 28% for sub-$25,000 pricing. This drove 16% sequential battery COGS cuts.

Second, scale at our Gigafactories: unabsorbed overhead fell to $950 per vehicle at over 85% utilization. Gigacasting with 9,000-ton presses consolidated 70 stampings into three parts, cutting BIW 35% to $4,200 and cycle times sharply. Structural packs saved $1,200 per SUV, digital twins reduced downtime 28% and scrap to 1.1%, labor to 22 hours via cobots. IRA localization adds $800 per vehicle, Shanghai rebates 8%.

Third, next-gen engineering: R&D down 11% to $1.1 billion, BEV3 skateboard cuts ECUs 60% to 48 with Nvidia chips, trimming BOM $900; standardized 400V architectures and SiC inverters boost efficiency 5%, lowering amortization $450 per vehicle.

Fourth, overhead trimmed 14% to 6.2% of revenue, headcount down 8%, AI automating procurement.

Holistically, $15,700 gross profit per vehicle, positioning for 25%+ margins at 1.2 million units in 2025, entering vans.

After me, we'll hear from Morgan Lee regarding our technological advancements.

Morgan Lee:
Thank you, Riley. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We are committed to developing cutting-edge solutions that will shape the future of mobility.

Specifically, our focus on electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains has delivered standout results, fueling 28% YoY delivery growth. Flagship Elysium sedan now at 482 miles EPA range, up 15% from 420, with 102 kWh LFP-NMC packs at 95% Nevada production. Fleet energy consumption down 12% to 198 Wh/mi, best-in-class versus Tesla Model S at 215 Wh/mi or Lucid at 208 Wh/mi. Apex R1 truck hits 415 miles EPA, 390 real-world highway.

This comes from 46-series cylindrical cells with silicon-graphene anodes at 850 Wh/L density, up from 720, dry electrode dropping costs to $92/kWh toward sub-$80. Cycle life over 1,500 equivalents. Axial-flux motors at 98.2% efficiency, AI dual-clutch e-transmission, 75% regen recapture, phase-change thermal holding temps within 2°C even in 115°F heat.

Aerodynamics at Cd 0.198 with active shutters and camera pods, mass down 7% to 4,120 lbs via gigacast and carbon fiber. In U.S., 14% share in $60K+ segment, 22% TCO savings for fleets; Europe WLTP 780 km aids CO2 targets, up 42%; China CLTC over 1,000 km for premiums.

Vertical integration to 40 GWh by 2026 de-risks volatility, sets solid-state path to 650 miles at 160 Wh/mi. Every 10-mile gain adds $1,200 ASP, 2.5 points margins—Q3 at 24.1%.

Following me, Casey Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Casey Patel:
Thank you, Morgan. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure the reliable flow of materials. Our focus on diversification and strategic partnerships has strengthened our supply chain resilience.

A critical headwind this quarter was raw material cost volatility and supply chain disruptions, pressuring gross margins 420 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 22.1%, despite 350,000 YTD deliveries of flagships like Apex sedan.

Raw materials dominate, batteries ~45% BOM. Lithium spot prices crashed 75% to $1,100/ton from Australian/South American gluts, but our NMC 811 cells held at $95/kWh, up 12% YoY via LG pass-throughs, shaving 150 bps margins. Nickel spiked 30% to $21,000/ton on Indonesian curbs (50% global supply), adding $120 million COGS overrun for mid-nickel cathodes. Cobalt stabilized at $28,000/ton, graphite up 25% to $12,000/ton on China issues; overall cell ASP up 14% to $135/kWh. Non-battery: aluminum up 8% to $2,800/ton, neodymium 22%, pushing vehicle materials to $28,500, up 11%.

Logistics: Red Sea attacks rerouted 30% shipments, freight up 150% to $12,000/FEU, delaying 15,000 Spartanburg units, missing 7% on 120,000 guidance. SiC MOSFETs at 22-week leads from Infineon/ST; UAW tightened steel to $750/ton.

Regionally: North America 65% deliveries, IRA U.S. content 55% for $7,500 credits, but Mexico copper up 10%; Europe 25%, CBAM adds 5%, Rotterdam delays; Asia 10%, yen weakness 12%. Buffers at 18 days cover, $250 million cost.

Financial hit: $380 million YoY COGS rise, EBITDA to 12.4%, FCF -$450 million. Peers like Tesla at 18.5%, Ford losses.

Response: 70% 2025 lithium/nickel hedged via Ganfeng/Tsingshan JVs at $12,000/ton nickel, $10/kWh cells; Nevada 4680 to 50 GWh at $70/kWh, yields 92%, cutting LG/CATL reliance to 60%; 40% LFP from BYD U.S., LMFP/sodium-ion pilots; Piedmont/Euro Manganese offtakes, Redwood recycling to 30% by 2027; Wolfspeed SiC localization, Berlin gigacasting 15% sheet savings.

Outlook: H1 2025 deflation to $110/kWh cells, normalizing logistics, 300-400 bps expansion to 25-26%, 500,000 deliveries, positive FCF. Our vertical strategy positions us for outperformance.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex for the Q&A session.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. [Operator Instructions]

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the total vehicle deliveries breakdown this quarter and how it compared to expectations?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks for the question. As I noted earlier, we delivered 152,450 vehicles globally in Q3, beating our 140,000 to 150,000 guidance and up 28% year-over-year from 118,900, with 12% sequential growth from Q2's 136,200. By model: Apex Terra SUV at 92,300 units, 60.6% mix, up 35% YoY on 520-mile range and Level 3 OTA; Vanguard Pickup 38,750, 25.4%, up 42% post-4680 certification to 600 miles, including 15,000 fleet; Ion Sedan and Zenith Luxury combined 21,400, 14%. Regionally: North America 110,200 or 72.3%, up 32%; Europe 28,500, 18.7%, up 18%; APAC ex-China 9,800, 6.4%, up 45%; China 3,950, 2.6%, down 5%. Backlog over 450,000, inventory lean at 12,000. Efficiency at 2.4 mi/kWh, outpacing market growth.

Analyst 2:
Great, and on revenue guidance for next quarter and FY2025, what are the biggest variables?

Taylor Voss:
Appreciate it. As detailed, Q3 revenue $2.9 billion up 32%, Q4 $3.2-3.4 billion on 185k-195k deliveries. FY2024 $12-12.5B, FY2025 $17-18.5B on 950k-1.02M units. Variables: U.S. IRA tailwinds, Europe subsidy dynamics, China stimulus; upside from software subs, downside port issues. Hedged and capitalized for execution.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Riley, how effective have the cost reduction initiatives been, especially manufacturing?

Riley Kim:
Yes, very effective—18% YoY COGS drop to $32,500/vehicle, $2.8B savings. Supply chain localization 22% cell cuts, gigacasting 35% BIW savings, structural packs $1,200 less, automation 28% less downtime. Q4 embeds 8-10% further reductions toward 25% margins.

Analyst 4:
Morgan, can you expand on the range and efficiency improvements driving demand?

Morgan Lee:
Absolutely. Elysium 482 miles up 15%, fleet 198 Wh/mi down 12%, via silicon anodes 850 Wh/L, 98% motors, Cd 0.198, 7% lighter. Resonating in U.S. fleets 22% TCO edge, Europe CO2 compliance, fueling 28% growth.

Analyst 5:
Casey, details on raw material impacts and mitigation?

Casey Patel:
Headwinds shaved 420 bps margins: lithium steady at $95/kWh despite spot crash, nickel +30% $120M hit, Red Sea +150% freight delaying 15k units. Mitigated with 70% hedges, 4680 ramp to $70/kWh, LFP shift, recycling—sets 300-400 bps recovery.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 6:
Final one: gross margin guidance and delivery by model outlook?

Taylor Voss:
Q4 22-24%, FY2025 25-27% on volume leverage 40%, ASP stability, COGS -15% from $85/kWh cells, IRA $12k/vehicle. By model: 3/Y 125-135k Q4, CyberForge 22-24k, etc., to 1M+ FY2025.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the ElectroDrive Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Impact of raw material costs and supply chain disruptions
Revenue guidance for the next quarter/year
Cost reduction initiatives and their effectiveness
Electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains
Gross margin guidance and key assumptions

aspect_summary.Cost reduction initiatives and their eff: Initiatives delivered 18% YoY COGS reduction to $32,500/vehicle and $2.8B run-rate savings via supply chain localization (22% cell cost cuts to $87/kWh), gigacasting (35% BIW savings), scale efficiencies (85%+ utilization), next-gen engineering, and 14% overhead trim; exceeded targets, positioning for 25%+ margins.
aspect_summary.Electric vehicle range improvements and: Elysium sedan: 482 miles EPA (+15% from 420); Apex R1 truck: 415 miles; fleet energy consumption: 198 Wh/mi (-12% YoY); achieved via silicon-graphene anodes (850 Wh/L density), 98.2% efficient axial-flux motors, Cd 0.198 aerodynamics, 7% mass reduction to 4,120 lbs.
aspect_summary.Gross margin guidance and key assumption: FY2024: 20-21%; Q4 2024: 22-24%; FY2025: 25-27%; assumes delivery growth to 720k-730k (FY2024)/950k-1.02M (FY2025), COGS declines 12-15% to $55k/vehicle, $85-90/kWh batteries, gigacasting/body cost reductions by 30%, IRA credits ~$12k/U.S. vehicle, premium mix, 75% North American content.
aspect_summary.Delivery volume guidance by model: Q4 2024: Model 3/Y equivalents 125k-135k (68% mix), Premium S/7X 32k-36k (+42% YoY), CyberForge pickup 22k-24k (+150% YoY), NovaOne affordable EV 3k-4k; FY2025: total 950k-1.02M, NovaOne scaling to 80k.
